mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts a compression of discount rates, which increases the present value of future equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over 3 months signals accommodative monetary policy, which increases the present value of equity cash flows and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 5,000 jobs predicts rising labor market confidence, which reduces risk premia and increases S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strengthening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
